'''''Dark Horse''''' is the sixth studio album by the Canadian [[Rock music|rock]] band [[Nickelback]], released on November 19, 2008.{{cite news |url=http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/news/story.aspx?newsitemID=19507 |title=Major Nickelback Announcement |publisher=[[Roadrunner Records]] |date=25 September 2008 |access-date=27 September 2008}} It is the follow-up to their Diamond-certified ''[[All the Right Reasons]]'' (2005). It was co-produced by the band and producer and songwriter [[Mutt Lange|Robert John "Mutt" Lange]], known for working with such acts as [[Foreigner (band)|Foreigner]], [[AC/DC]], [[Bryan Adams]], [[Def Leppard]] and [[Shania Twain]]. ''Dark Horse'' sold 326,000 in its first week and debuted at number two in the US. More than a year after its release, the album did not leave the top 100 on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]]. In its 91st week, the album peaked at number 46 for the week of August 28, 2010.[{{BillboardURLbyName|artist=nickelback|chart=Billboard 200}} Dark Horse climbs on the Billboard 200 Albums and crack 80 consecutive weeks] 'Billboard' Accessed on May 13, 2010. The album spent 125 consecutive weeks inside the ''Billboard'' 200.{{cite magazine |url={{BillboardURLbyName|artist=nickelback|chart=all}} |title=Dark Horse - Nickelback > Album Info |magazine=Billboard.com |access-date=September 22, 2011}} It was ranked at number 191 on ''Billboard''{{'}}s ''200 Albums of the Decade''.{{cite magazine |url=http://www.billboard.com/#/charts-decade-end/billboard-200-albums?year=2009&begin=181&order=position |title=Best of the 2000s: Billboard 200 Albums |at=Showing 181-200 |magazine=Billboard.com |access-date=September 22, 2011}} It is also the band's fourth straight multi-Platinum selling album in the United States. As of 2010, the album has sold three million copies in the United States and five million copies worldwide. ==Promotion and singles== The first single from the album was "[[Gotta Be Somebody]]", which was released online for free [[Music download|digital download]] on September 29, 2008, for a strict 24-hour period. "[[If Today Was Your Last Day]]" had been planned as the lead single but was scrapped at the last minute. The track "[[Something in Your Mouth]]" became available for download from the United States [[iTunes Store]] on October 28, and was released to US rock radio airplay as the second single from the album on December 15. The song was a hit in 2009 in many countries, such as the United States. In Australia, it received little airplay. In January 2009, the album's second mainstream single (third overall) was released: "[[I'd Come for You]]", with [[Nigel Dick]] having made the [[music video]]. Songs "Something in Your Mouth" and "[[Burn It to the Ground]]", written by Kroeger, were released only to the [[Rock music|rock radio stations]] in December 2008 and May 2009 respectively. The exclusive [[Walmart]] edition of ''Dark Horse'' included a link to download an MP3 from Nickelback's performance of "This Afternoon" on [[Walmart Soundcheck]].{{cite web |url=http://www.walmart.com/catalog/product.do?product_id=10721070 |title=Nickelback - CD: Dark Horse (with Exclusive MP3 Download) |publisher=[[Walmart]]}} The album won numerous accolades at the 2009 [[Juno Awards]], winning three out of five of its nominated awards including "Rock Album of the Year". ''Dark Horse'' was certified [[RIAA certification|Platinum]] by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA) on December 9, 2008, only three weeks after its North American release. The album also remained in the top 20 on the ''Billboard'' 200 for weeks after its release.[https://web.archive.org/web/20051101063637/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/riaa/index.jsp Latest Platinum Album Certifications]. [[billboard.com]]. Accessed on 15 December 2008.{{cite web| url=http://riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?resultpage=1&table=SEARCH_RESULTS&action=&title=Dark%20Horse&artist=nickelback&format=&debutLP=&category=&sex=&releaseDate=&requestNo=&type=&level=&label=&company=&certificationDate=&awardDescription=&catalogNo=&aSex=&rec_id=&charField=&gold=&platinum=&multiPlat=&level2=&certDate=&album=&id=&after=&before=&startMonth=1&endMonth=1&startYear=1958&endYear=2009&sort=Artist&perPage=25 | title=Gold and Platinum Database Search | website=[[Recording Industry Association of America]] | access-date=15 December 2008}} The album was certified 2× Platinum in April 2009, and had by April 2010 sold over three million copies in the US. "Burn It to the Ground" was also nominated for Best Hard Rock Performance at the [[52nd Annual Grammy Awards|52nd Grammy Awards]] but lost to [[AC/DC]]'s "War Machine". On September 13, 2010, the album re-entered the [[German Albums Chart]] at number 30, 21 months after its debut and almost six months after its last entry on that chart.{{cite web |url=http://musicline.de/de/chartverfolgung_summary/title/NICKELBACK/Dark+Horse/longplay |language=de |title=Nickelback: Dark Horse |publisher=musicline.de |access-date=September 22, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120831214817/http://musicline.de/de/chartverfolgung_summary/title/NICKELBACK/Dark+Horse/longplay |archive-date=2012-08-31 |url-status=dead}} == Music and lyrics == Lyrically, ''Dark Horse'' has been characterized as "a slice of perceptive, precise self-examination". Some of the subject matter is considered to be [[Vulgarity|vulgar]], and by the assessment of some critics, [[Misogyny|misogynistic]]. Themes explored include [[binge drinking]], [[recreational drug use]], [[Prostitution|prostitutes]], [[Pornographic film actor|adult film actresses]], and [[Stripper|exotic dancers]].{{Citation |title=Dark Horse - Nickelback {{!}} Album {{!}} AllMusic |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/dark-horse-mw0000801795 |access-date=2025-06-23 |language=en}}{{Cite news |last=Sullivan |first=Caroline |date=2008-11-14 |title=Rock review: Nickelback, Dark Horse |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2008/nov/14/nickelback-dark-horse-review |access-date=2025-06-23 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}{{Cite web |title=Album Review: Dark Horse |url=http://consequenceofsound.net/2008/11/26/album-review-dark-horse/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081205081730/http://consequenceofsound.net/2008/11/26/album-review-dark-horse/ |archive-date=2008-12-05 |access-date=2025-06-23 |website=consequenceofsound.net |language=en}} Some of ''Dark Horse''{{'}}s guitar riffs have been described as "[[wiktionary:knuckle-dragging|knuckle-dragging]]". The album's production has been described as "caught somewhere between the two extremes of [[AC/DC]] and [[Def Leppard]]". The album incorporates [[Loop (music)|drum loops]] on some tracks. The album contains elements of [[Honky-tonk|honkey-tonk music]], namely in the track "[[This Afternoon]]".{{Cite web |title=Dark Horse - Blender |url=http://www.blender.com/guide/new/55373/dark-horse.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101229062224/http://www.blender.com/guide/new/55373/dark-horse.html |archive-date=2010-12-29 Staff writer David Buchanan assessed: "The problem is that while Nickelback's front man tries so hard to convert us to [[perversion]], it feels less like [[Matthew McConaughey]] hitting on you and more like those creepy old men at your local burger joint. Chad Kroeger might be blond now, but he still sounds like a sex-crazed 40-something with a soft side". ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' gave the album a positive review, complimenting its production, writing "[[Mutt Lange]] lightens Nickelback's dreary post-grunge plod, applying guitar shimmer to prom ballads and detonating big beats under frat-party shouts and raplike vocal parts".{{cite magazine |first=Chuck |last=Eddy |title=Review: ''Dark Horse'' |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/albumreviews/dark-horse-20081127|date=27 November 2008 |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |access-date=5 July 2011}} Whilst ''[[ChartAttack]]'' credited the band's success to knowing its target audience: "Chad Kroeger is a genius because he knows exactly what people want and precisely how far he can go. He turned out an extremely racy album that's loaded with songs about gettin' drunk and doin' it all without breaking any taboos, and with enough love and [[moral authority]] to grease its passage into the mainstream. Rejoice, North America. This is your world".{{cite web |url=http://www.chartattack.com/reviews/62848/nickelbacks-dark-horse-for-dark-times |title=Nickelback's Dark Horse For Dark Times |first=Evan |last=Dickson |date=November 17, 2008 |publisher=chartattack.com |access-date=September 22, 2011 |archive-date=December 17, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081217033035/http://www.chartattack.com/reviews/62848/nickelbacks-dark-horse-for-dark-times |url-status=usurped}} ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' also praised the album's content: "The bulletproof Nickelback provides affordable fun that promises good returns in hard times".[http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/reviews-album/dark-horse-1003895507.story Billboard review] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090330043741/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/reviews-album/dark-horse-1003895507.story |date=March 30, 2009}} ==Track listing== {{Track listing | all_lyrics = [[Chad Kroeger]] | all_music = [[Nickelback]] with [[Mutt Lange|Robert John "Mutt" Lange]] on tracks 1, 4, 7, 8 and 11 and [[Joey Moi]] on tracks 1, 2 and 8. | title1 = [[Something in Your Mouth]] | length1 = 3:39 | title2 = [[Burn It to the Ground]] | length2 = 3:32 | title3 = [[Gotta Be Somebody]] | length3 = 4:12 | title4 = [[I'd Come for You]] | length4 = 4:22 | title5 = Next Go Round | length5 = 3:43 | title6 = Just to Get High | length6 = 4:02 | title7 = [[Never Gonna Be Alone]] | length7 = 3:47 | title8 = [[Shakin' Hands]] | length8 = 3:39 | title9 = S.E.X. | length9 = 3:53 | title10 = [[If Today Was Your Last Day]] | length10 = 4:09 | title11 = [[This Afternoon]] | length11 = 4:33 |total_length = 43:36 }} '''[[Walmart]] exclusive digital download bonus track''' #
